snippet: The S&P 500 rose almost 15 percent for the three months through June, and many stock analysts remain optimistic that corporate earnings driven by artificial intelligence will keep growing.

headline: Prominent Tech Founder in Indonesia Is Found Guilty in Corruption Case
snippet: The case against Nadiem Makarim, a co-founder of Gojek, has fueled concerns about judicial fairness in a nation where foreign investors were already growing wary.

headline: N.I.H. Announces World’s Largest Integrated Health Database
snippet: It contains more than half a million people’s genomes, paired with clinical records and wearable tech data. That gives researchers unmatched power to study both diseases and treatments.

headline: BMW Will Build a New Electric S.U.V. in South Carolina
snippet: The German company is doubling down on electric vehicles even as other automakers pull back after acknowledging billions of dollars in losses.

headline: The Company Reviving AOL, Vimeo and Other Internet Oldies Amid the A.I. Boom
snippet: Bending Spoons, an Italian company that buys aging internet companies, is going public this week at a potential value of $19 billion.

headline: Comcast and NBCUniversal Will Go It Alone. But for How Long?
snippet: Almost as soon as the two companies announced a split, analysts rushed to consider potential merger and acquisition targets for each.

headline: C.I.A. Reorganization Prioritizes Cyberoperations
snippet: John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, said that the agency would take “smart risks,” but that people would have oversight of artificial intelligence.

headline: Independent Studio Buys Movie About OpenAI That Amazon Dropped
snippet: Neon purchased “Artificial,” which focuses on OpenAI’s chief, Sam Altman, after Amazon walked away from it following an investment in the start-up.

headline: China’s Plan to Save Jobs From A.I.
snippet: As it embeds the technology in every industry, China is thinking about how to keep humans employed.
